louisiana.title: Louisiana Purchase, 1803
louisiana.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
louisiana.supports: Purchase from France in 1803; about 530 million acres for $15 million.

erie.title: Today in History - October 26 (Erie Canal)
erie.supports: Erie Canal opened October 26, 1825 between the Hudson River and Lake Erie.

texas.title: Texas Annexation, 1845
texas.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
texas.supports: Texas admitted to the United States on December 29, 1845.

goldrush.supports: News of gold brought approximately 300,000 people to California (rough, commonly cited estimate).

goldrush_loc.supports: About 300,000 people arrived during the Gold Rush period.

homestead.title: Homestead Act (1862)
homestead.supports: Passed May 20, 1862; 160 acres of surveyed public land for a small fee and five years' residence.

golden_spike.title: The Last Spike: History at a Glance
golden_spike.publisher: National Park Service, Golden Spike NHP
golden_spike.supports: Central Pacific (Sacramento) and Union Pacific (Omaha) joined at Promontory Summit, Utah, May 10, 1869.

frontier.title: Following the Frontier Line, 1790 to 1890
frontier.supports: Census Bureau visualization of the frontier line (settled area, 2+ people per square mile); the 1890 Census said there could hardly be said to be a frontier line any more.

ellis.title: Ellis Island Chronology
ellis.supports: Opened January 1, 1892; over 12 million future Americans received 1892-1954.

greatmig.title: The Great Migration (1910-1970)
greatmig.supports: Roughly 1910s-1970s; approximately six million Black people moved from the South to the North, Midwest and West.

dustbowl.title: Route 66: 1926-1945
dustbowl.supports: Cites an estimate that 210,000 people migrated to California to escape the Dust Bowl.

interstate.title: National Interstate and Defense Highways Act (1956)
interstate.supports: Signed June 29, 1956; authorized 41,000 miles of Interstate highways.

railmaps.title: Railroad Maps, 1828 to 1900
railmaps.supports: General reference for the growth of the U.S. rail network; routes in the video are simplified.
